title: Rolling telemetry-driven mini-cohorts for pinned model updates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood customers pin model versions to control quality and compliance. We need a safer way to expose new model revisions behind a pin that reduces blast radius while providing richer signal for quality and performance decisions. Existing canary approaches are traffic-percent driven and often fail to isolate cohort-specific regressions (e.g., token distribution, latency tails for long-context requests).

Proposal summary:
Introduce 'mini-cohorts' — small, rolling, telemetry-driven user cohorts created as stable routing groups behind a pin. Each mini-cohort receives a configurable fraction of the pin's traffic and is instrumented with an expanded telemetry surface (per-cohort request/response sampling, latency percentile breakdowns by input length, semantic-quality checks against golden prompts, and token-cost accounting). Cohorts rotate and expand based on signals: if a cohort's quality and latency metrics remain within thresholds for N observation windows, its traffic share increases; failing cohorts are automatically scaled down and routed to the previous pinned revision.

Goals:
- Reduce risk of model-quality regressions slipping into full traffic for pinned updates.
- Surface cohort-level regressions that aggregate by product, prompt shape, or customer segment.
- Provide an automated, observable progression from 1% -> 25% -> 50% for safe rollouts with automated fallback.

Key design elements:
1) Cohort selection: support both user-id hashing and request-attribute buckets (e.g., route, dataset tag, enterprise customer flag). Cohorts are persistent for 24h by default to avoid flapping.
2) Telemetry expansion: cohort-level nyquist sampling of responses (configurable rate) with structured evals against a small golden set plus automated checks (toxicity, hallucination score, acceptance rate).
3) Signal-driven progression policy: composite gate combining quality (golden pass rate >= 98%), latency (p95 <= baseline + 120ms), and cost delta (per-token increase <= 10%).
4) Automated rollback: failing cohorts are instantly routed back to the pinned baseline and an incident ticket is created with prefilled diagnostics.
5) Opt-in API fields: allow customers to enable mini-cohorts on their pins with default conservative thresholds.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (lab): implement telemetry schema and golden-set eval runner. Validate on internal prompts and SRE test workloads. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (internal beta): enable for Redwood internal product routes to verify cohort stability and dashboarding. (3 weeks)
- Phase 2 (customer beta): invite 6 enterprise customers with Dedicated instances and select hosted customers to opt in. Monitor for 4 weeks.
- Phase 3 (general availability): expose as a pin option in Console + API, default off for existing pins.

Metrics to monitor:
- Per-cohort: golden-set pass rate, p50/p95 latency, request success rate, token cost per request.
- Platform: number of active cohorts, automated rollbacks, time-to-detect regressions, false-positive rate for rollback triggers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary pipeline runs produce cohort-level dashboards with stable sampling for >95% of requests in cohort window.
- Automation safely progresses at least 80% of successful cohorts from 1% to 25% in the test environment without operator intervention.
- No customer-facing incidents attributable to cohort routing in the customer beta group for 4 consecutive weeks.
- Documentation and Console UI flows implemented for enabling, thresholds, and manual override.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overaggressive rollout due to noisy signals. Mitigation: ensemble gating combining multiple independent signals, conservative default thresholds, minimum observation windows.
- Risk: Telemetry cost increase for high-volume customers. Mitigation: configurable sampling rate and golden set size per customer; default low-cost sampling.
- Risk: Cohort churn undermines analysis. Mitigation: cohort stickiness and minimum lifetime of 24h; metrics normalized by cohort age.

Dependencies and open questions:
- ENG: implement cohort routing primitives and durable cohort membership. (ENG-2987)
- Console: UI for cohort config and manual controls (design ticket to be created).
- Instrumentation: need efficient per-cohort sampling and structured eval pipeline.
- Legal/security: verify telemetry payloads against PII policy for enterprise pins.

Deliverables:
- API extension to enable mini-cohorts on pins and configure progression policy.
- Console pages: cohort list, cohort detail pages with expanded telemetry, manual override controls.
- Playbooks: automated rollback notification, post-rollout quality checklist.

Next steps:
- PM to align scope with Eng in planning meeting (2026-03-05).
- Engineering spike for telemetry cost projection and data model (one week).
- Design kickoff for Console flows (2026-03-08).
acceptance_criteria: Cohort routing primitives implemented and tested in staging

Progression automation moves successful cohorts from 1% to 25% in staging for >=80% of runs

Console UI for enabling mini-cohorts with manual override is available in beta
